item.content:encoded:
Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa will appear on fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan at 7pm tonight.

The show will focus on the state of preparedness of the Fijian Elections Office for the proposed national referendum on December 9th and the next general elections which has to be held by February 6th 2027, the nationwide voter registration underway, changes to the electoral laws and the impact on the voters and the country, and the impact of any drastic changes with two months to go for the last day for the Writ of Elections to be issued on December 24th 2026 amongst other issues.

You can watch the Straight Talk interview on our facebook page, TikTok, YouTube and Instagram accounts.

You can also check out the podcast, fijivillage Straight Talk With Vijay Narayan on Spotify and Apple podcasts.

item.title: No mining or dredging on our land - Tikina Nasigatoka spokesperson
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/10/2026 The people of Tikina Nasigatoka are objecting to the proposed iron-sands mining project in Sigatoka.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/10/2026

The people of Tikina Nasigatoka are objecting to the proposed iron-sands mining project in Sigatoka.

Tikina Nasigatoka spokesperson Joeli Kunaturaga says this is the third time they have objected to the proposed project.

He says they first objected in 2018 and again last year, when they raised their concerns with the late former Minister for Agriculture, Vatimi Rayalu.

Kunaturaga says they also raised their objections with Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, Opposition Leader Inia Seruiratu, Minister for Lands Filimoni Vosarogo and Minister for iTaukei Affairs Ifereimi Vasu earlier this year.

He adds that they have not received any feedback from the government regarding their concerns.

He further adds that after 15 months, the government presented the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report, but he is concerned that they were neither informed nor consulted on the matter.

The spokesperson says they do not want dredging or mining on their land because they are concerned about future generations.

Kunaturaga says they made their position clear to the government in 2024 that they do not want any mining or dredging on their land and do not agree to the waiver of their fishing rights.

He is also calling on the people of Nadroga/Navosa Province to support their objections for the betterment of the province.

Meanwhile, the deadline for submissions to the Department of Environment for the proposed Special Prospecting License 1495, Kulukulu Sand, Sigatoka Iron-sands project by Magma Mines Pte Limited is October 30th.

item.title: El Niño effects continue to intensify in Lautoka as students and farmers suffer
item.description: The effects of El Niño continue to intensify, with Lautoka residents saying the water situation has worsened over the past four to five months, leaving some communities without water for days and affecting students preparing for their exams. Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka Residents and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says the situation has worsened, affecting students who are
item.content:encoded:
The effects of El Niño continue to intensify, with Lautoka residents saying the water situation has worsened over the past four to five months, leaving some communities without water for days and affecting students preparing for their exams.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka Residents and Ratepayers Association President Narayan Reddy says the situation has worsened, affecting students who are preparing for their examinations.

Reddy says some students have reported wearing the same school uniform for two to three days because they do not have enough water to wash their clothes.

Insert:Reddy on affected students 21st Oct

He says residents in interior parts of Lautoka, including Tavakubu and Saru, are experiencing water shortages, with some going without supply for three to four days.

Reddy says the river that many residents rely on for water has also dried up, making life even more difficult for affected communities.

He says the supply of vegetables has also decreased due to El Niño, resulting in a significant increase in prices.

Meanwhile, Reddy says livestock farmers have been forced to sell many of their goats and cows because of the lack of water, while some animals are dying.

He is calling on the Government to provide water to communities in Lautoka that are experiencing shortages.

item.title: iTaukei should retain the name Fijian if they wish – Nand
item.description: Nand says what matters to him is that people's identities and nationality are recognised in official documents, including birth certificates and passports. He also called for the Great Council of Chiefs to be retained, saying it has played an important role in protecting iTaukei traditions and village protocols for many years.
item.content:encoded:
Nand says what matters to him is that people's identities and nationality are recognised in official documents, including birth certificates and passports.

He also called for the Great Council of Chiefs to be retained, saying it has played an important role in protecting iTaukei traditions and village protocols for many years.

Nand believes the Council should continue to play a role in deciding who becomes Fiji's President, and that the position should be held by an indigenous Fijian.

On whether Fiji should be a secular or Christian state, Nand says Fiji is a multiracial country where people follow different religions.

He believes politics should be kept separate from religious beliefs, including Christianity and Hinduism.

Nand also highlighted the friendliness of Fiji's people, saying it is one of the reasons foreigners choose to live and invest in the country.

item.content:encoded:
Minister for Information and Environment, Lynda Tabuya is one of the candidates being considered for the position of Attorney-General, with Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka confirming that a list of potential candidates is currently being vetted by the Solicitor-General.

Rabuka says the Government is looking at several possibilities to fill the position and is assessing whether the candidates have the necessary legal qualifications and experience to lead the office.

He says the role requires a high level of legal maturity and that several experienced lawyers are being considered.

When asked whether Tabuya was among the candidates, Rabuka said she could be one of them.

He has not confirmed when the appointment will be announced, saying the public will know when he makes the announcement.
